_readme: Tracks which verticals' situation rooms actually call TSMMemory.registerAnomaly() and therefore show up in RCM OS's Cross-Module Exceptions (Executive tab). 'wired' = confirmed registerAnomaly() call site exists. 'partial' = the page uses TSMMemory (exposure/narrative/timeline) but does not yet register anomalies. 'not_started' = no TSMMemory usage found. Update this file whenever a vertical's adoption status changes so it stays a source of truth instead of tribal knowledge.
sector_key_reference: Sector is auto-detected from the page URL path in tsm-memory-engine.js's detectSector() — codes below must match those keys exactly (construction, healthcare, insurance, finops, legal, tax, bpo, reo, rrd, music, executive).

finops.notes: Original 3 rooms from the Cross-Module Exceptions launch (Compliance, Vendor, Logistics), plus working-capital-calculator now also registering.

construction.notes: Executive/strategist portals not yet confirmed wired — only the war room.

bpo.notes: bpo-executive-portal.html and bpo-strategist.html use TSMMemory/TSMExceptions for the P1/P2/P3 exception queue (a separate, older mechanism) — not yet unified with registerAnomaly. Worth reconciling so BPO exceptions surface in RCM OS too, not just its own portal.

healthcare.notes: hc-main-strategist.html and memory-timeline/memory.engine components use TSMMemory for exposure/narrative/timeline. No registerAnomaly() call site found yet — denial/payer-delay detections don't currently reach Cross-Module Exceptions.

insurance.notes: insurance-executive-portal.html uses TSMMemory but no registerAnomaly() call site found yet.

legal.notes: legal-executive-portal.html uses TSMMemory but no registerAnomaly() call site found yet.

reo.notes: re-exec-portal.html uses TSMMemory but no registerAnomaly() call site found yet.

onboarding_checklist: 1. Confirm the page's URL path matches an existing detectSector() branch in tsm-memory-engine.js (or add a new one) so anomalies land under the right sector key.

2. At the point a vertical's own detection logic finds something wrong (a threshold breach, a missing required field, a failed check), call window.TSMMemory.registerAnomaly({ entityType, entityId, anomalyCode, title, severity, source }). anomalyCode should use this vertical's codePrefix (e.g. HC-DENIAL-THRESHOLD) so codes never collide across verticals.

3. Severity must be one of CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW — CRITICAL auto-opens a Mission Core mission from the RCM OS Executive tab, so reserve it for things that actually need someone paged, not just flagged.

4. No new relay domain or mission vertical needed — RCM OS's Cross-Module Exceptions block reads every sector automatically via TSMMemory.getCrossModuleAnomalies(). Once step 2 ships, the vertical shows up there with zero RCM OS-side changes.
5. Update this file's status for the vertical from partial/not_started to wired, and list the actual source file(s).
known_gaps: All of this still lives in browser localStorage (TSM_OPERATIONAL_MEMORY_V3) — per-machine, not server-synced. A fresh browser or different laptop won't see anomalies until it visits the source pages itself. Server-sync is tracked as future work, not done.
No resolution workflow yet: closing the underlying issue in a source room doesn't auto-clear the anomaly in RCM OS's Executive tab.
BPO runs a separate, older exception mechanism (TSMExceptions / bpoFeedExceptions) for its own P1/P2/P3 queue that predates registerAnomaly() and isn't unified with it yet.
